titleText.es: Por un lado, nunca podrás convencer a tus padres de que se cambien. Por otro lado, ¡nunca podrás convencer a tus padres de que se cambien!
titleText.en: On one hand, you'll never be able to convince your parents to switch. On the other hand, you'll never be able to convince your parents to switch!
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official English title attributes are preserved exactly. The raster treats GOOGLE+ and both FACEBOOK labels as product names, while the localized CLIC remains a Spanish sound word. Vision omitted GOOGLE+, A, CLIC, and several punctuation-sensitive letters in the opening exchange.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Unirte combines the dictionary form unir with te because the action is directed back to one familiar listener. A normally follows when the group, service, or activity being joined is named.

example.en: You can join the club tomorrow.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce something you suppose or guess?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use supongo que, then state the idea.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Supongo is the form used by the speaker, and que introduces the belief that follows. The expression often sounds less certain than creo que.

example.en: I suppose she will arrive soon.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: unirte · como · qué demonios · en realidad
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does the final change of mind make the social-network exchange a joke?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The listener first resists a new service because it is described as Facebook, then suddenly realizes that a Facebook-like service was what he wanted.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Google+ launched as a social network in 2011 and was commonly compared with Facebook. The blank middle panel gives the listener time to reconsider. The official title text adds a two-sided joke: parents being hard to persuade to switch is both a disadvantage and an advantage of a new network.

applications.explanationEn: Supongo presents the speaker's tentative conclusion, and que introduces the idea that follows.
Todo lo que introduces the complete set of what the speaker wanted, and quería supplies the past desire.
Quería presents the desire as an ongoing past state rather than a single completed event.
En realidad marks the contrast between the speaker's first reaction and what he actually wanted.
